issues.t: Air suspension springs leak and the car sags
issues.sym: One corner or the whole car sits low, often after being parked overnight. You may see a suspension warning, a lean to one side, or a message that the car is too low to drive.
issues.why: Every US Phaeton rides on air springs (air struts). Their rubber bellows age and crack, and the air lines and fittings can leak, so the springs slowly lose pressure. A strut can also burst outright.
issues.next: Don't drive far with a corner sitting on its bump stops; it can damage tires and the compressor. Have a shop that knows VW/Audi air suspension find the leak. Replacing the worn spring usually fixes it, and many owners replace them in pairs.

issues.sym: A suspension warning light, a car that won't lift back up after sitting, or a compressor under the car that runs loudly or for a long time.
issues.why: The compressor has to work harder and longer when a spring or line leaks. Over time it overheats and wears out, and its relay can fail with it.
issues.next: Fix any air leak first, or a new compressor will fail early too. A shop can test compressor output and the relay before replacing parts.

issues.t: Engine overheating from cooling system failures
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, a coolant warning appears, or the engine overheats on the highway. You may notice a sweet coolant smell or low coolant.
issues.why: Aging cooling parts are a known weak spot on these cars. A sticking thermostat, worn water pump, clogged radiator or failed coolant valves can all stop the engine from shedding heat.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the gauge reaches red; overheating can ruin these engines. Don't open a hot coolant cap. Have the cooling system pressure-tested and the thermostat and water pump checked.

issues.sym: The trunk won't open with the button or remote, the power trunk acts up, or tail lights, the license plate light or the trunk release stop working.
issues.why: The wires that run through the flexible tube into the trunk lid bend every time the trunk opens. Their protective sleeve wears through and the wires crack or corrode. VW issued a service bulletin with a repair harness for this.
issues.next: Get it repaired soon, because broken wires can also disable lights and the inside trunk escape release. A shop can splice in VW's repair harness or replace the loom.

issues.sym: The car won't start after sitting, the battery is flat overnight, or features such as seat heaters, the stereo or climate control switch off by themselves with a message.
issues.why: The Phaeton has two batteries in the trunk and many control modules that draw power. When the batteries are weak or something stays awake, the car's load-management system shuts off comfort features to protect starting power. VW issued bulletins about this shutdown and no-start.
issues.next: Have both batteries load-tested and the charging system checked. If new batteries keep going flat, a shop should measure parasitic drain to find the module that stays awake.

issues.t: Water damage to keyless entry module from clogged sunroof drains
issues.sym: Damp or wet carpet in the passenger footwell, then keyless entry or push-button start that stops working, or odd electrical faults.
issues.why: Leaves block the sunroof drain tubes, so rainwater overflows into the cabin. The keyless-entry (KESSY) control module sits under the passenger footwell carpet and can be ruined by the water.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains and dry the carpet right away. If keyless functions have failed, a VW/Audi specialist can test and replace the module.

issues.t: Power steering lines rust and leak
issues.sym: Red or brown fluid drips near the front passenger wheel, a low power steering fluid level, or a whining pump and heavier steering.
issues.why: The steel power steering lines corrode, most often in the passenger-side wheel arch, until they leak.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and don't let the pump run dry. Have the lines inspected; the fix is a new line or a repaired section.

issues.sym: A whining or moaning noise that rises with engine speed, most noticeable when turning the wheel.
issues.why: Owners report the power steering pump getting noisy with age, often because of low fluid from a leak or internal wear.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks first. If the level is fine and the noise continues, have the pump checked before steering assist fails.

issues.t: Suspension control arm bushings wear and knock
issues.sym: Knocking or clunking from the front over bumps, loose or vague steering, or uneven tire wear.
issues.why: This heavy car wears out the rubber bushings in its upper and lower control arms. Owners also report corrosion in the arms letting metal parts touch.
issues.next: Have the front suspension inspected. Replacing worn control arms or bushings and then getting an alignment usually fixes the noise.

issues.sym: A window that won't move, moves slowly, makes grinding or clicking noises, or drops or slides off its track.
issues.why: The window regulators and motors wear out, especially on the rear doors. Owner repair records show regulator replacements even at low mileage.
issues.next: Keep the window closed if you can and avoid running a stuck motor repeatedly. A shop can replace the regulator and motor.

issues.t: Climate control vents and flaps stop working
issues.sym: Air only comes out of some vents, a dash vent door stays open or closed, or changing the climate settings does nothing.
issues.why: The Phaeton uses small electric motors to open and close its vent doors and air flaps. These motors and the climate electronics can fail with age.
issues.next: Have the climate control fault codes read to find which flap motor has failed. It's a comfort issue, but get it fixed if you lose defrost.

issues.sym: A check engine light, a temperature gauge that reads wrong, poor running when cold, or the fans running oddly.
issues.why: On the W12, the coolant temperature sensor at the back of the engine is a well-known failure, often around 100,000 miles. It is hard to reach, so the repair takes several hours.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A specialist can usually change the sensor by removing the intake manifold instead of pulling the engine.

issues.t: W12 coolant and breather hoses crack
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the car, a low coolant warning, a coolant smell, or an oil vapor leak around the engine.
issues.why: Small coolant hoses near the reservoir and front of the W12 become brittle with age, and the plastic oil vapor (breather) lines can crack too.
issues.next: Top up only with the right VW coolant, and have the leak found before the engine overheats. Brittle hoses are usually simple to replace.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat occupant sensor
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light stays on, or the passenger airbag status looks wrong.
issues.why: The passenger seat has a sensor that detects whether someone is sitting there. VW bulletins cover fault codes from this occupant detection system, including after the sensor or seat cushion is replaced.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon. The airbags may not work correctly while the light is on, so don't ignore it.

issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, a rough idle, shaking, or loss of power.
issues.why: VW issued a service action about ignition coils that can fail, which turns on the warning light and causes misfires and power loss.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, slow down and avoid hard driving. Have the misfire codes read; the bad coil is usually replaced along with spark plugs if they are due.

issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, shuddering when pulling away, or the transmission not shifting properly.
issues.why: Owners report torque converter faults and poor shifting, and older automatic transmissions on these cars can wear internally. Old fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned and the fluid level and condition checked. A fluid service and software adaptation sometimes helps; internal wear needs a specialist.

issues.sym: Paint bubbling or blistering on the doors or trunk lid, rust spots, or the plastic trim along the door bottoms sagging.
issues.why: VW bulletins describe hairline cracks and paint damage on front and rear doors that let moisture in. Owners also see the steel bar behind the lower door trim rust, so the trim drops.
issues.next: Have body shops treat blisters early before rust spreads. Sagging door trim is usually a simple fix.
